Pike Creek 10 Year Rum Barrel Finish

A light, sweet cask-influenced blend with a useful initial spice lift. Independent reports differ on improvement over port, while thinness and a short finish recur.

84 proof · 42% ABV10 YearsQuality 5.5Value 5.2Overall 5.3

The short version

A light, sweet cask-influenced blend with a useful initial spice lift. Independent reports differ on improvement over port, while thinness and a short finish recur.

Exact identity: Pike Creek ten-year Rum Barrel Finish / Double Barreled, 42% ABV / 84 proof, 750 mL; recurring rum-finished range introduced in 2016.

Background and history

Selfbuilt documents the switch from port to rum in September 2016 batches and the rise from 40% to 42%. Modern Double Barreled is the named pack, not a separate age-inferred product.

The verified producer photograph visibly carries the ten-year label despite a shorter catalogue title.

For the shared historical context, read Canadian whisky, cross-border trade and the American market. The release chronology above distinguishes the current bottle from its brand’s earlier history.

Producer, grains, aging and finishing

Current exact producer pack confirms ten years and 42%, with rum finishing after oak aging. Matched technical reporting describes double-column corn and once-column rye, initially ex-bourbon matured. TWS’s 2017 brand-session report names Guyana casks and 120 days; those details are attributed to that era, not claimed as an unchanged current schedule. No direct rum addition is authenticated.

Producer / source
Hiram Walker & Sons, Windsor, Ontario / Pernod Ricard; Corby Spirit & Wine brand stewardship
Grain / mash composition
Corn and rye; matched brand-representative reporting gives approximately 3% rye, not a universal ratio established for every current batch.
Strength
84 proof · 42% ABV
Age statement
10 Years
Finishing
Rum-cask finish after ex-bourbon maturation; 120-day Guyana-cask account attributed to 2017 reporting, current duration undisclosed.

Critical review synthesis

Selfbuilt · Selfbuilt’s Whisky Analysis

The initial rum batch has spice but less aromatic fruit than port, a watery body and a quick, slightly bitter ending.

Scope: November 8, 2016 purchased ten-year / 42%; single batch, not certified current consistency.

Bryan Vanderkruk · Toronto Whisky Society

The 2017 rum bottle is sweet and oaky with a short ending; the reviewer nevertheless prefers it to port.

Scope: September 21, 2017 exact rum section; adjacent 21-year Speyside is separate evidence.

Published sample evidence, not first-person tasting or a representative survey. Reviewer disagreement and recipe-era limitations remain explicit; publisher grades are not mechanically converted.

Quality and calibration

Quality 5.5 / 10. Above-average but modest provisional Canadian blend execution. Comfortable sweetness and some spice/body have support, but short persistence, watery texture and occasional bitterness reduce development and finish scores.

No defensible complete Canadian native 1/5/10 framework is established for this comparison group. Seven universal execution dimensions are assessed within Canadian Blended Whisky; unrelated American bourbon and straight-rye endpoints are not imported.

Calibration mode: evidence_limited_provisional. Evidence-limited provisional; matched independent tasting with sample and era limitations

Price, Value and Overall

USD 41.99 / 750 mL · Exact ten-year / 84-proof Caskers U.S. offer USD 41.99 / 750 mL · price context 2026-10-15; checked 2026-10-15.

Exact dated U.S. advertised consumer offer; no current NC ABC price or local stock claim. Tax, shipping and destination restrictions are separate.

Value 5.2 / 10. Modest Value at USD 41.99. The documented ten-year and rum treatment are useful specifications, but short finish and limited development weaken the proposition beside the current USD 39.99 Lot No. 40 core. A preference for softer, sweeter Canadian blends may still justify it.

Overall 5.3 / 10. Overall = √(Quality × Value). The index displays one decimal and sorts on the unrounded result. If either component lacks sufficient evidence, Overall is N/A.

Checked October 15, 2026. Prices are dated consumer references, not stock guarantees. Tax and delivery may change final cost. Canadian dollars are not converted into U.S. Cost.

Serving recommendations

Neat

Start with a small neat pour and assess development and texture against the attributed accounts.

Water / rocks

Add drops or one small cube gradually; compare texture before adding more dilution.

Old Fashioned

Taste before adding syrup, especially with sweet or wine-influenced expressions; recurring blends can be the cost comparison.

Manhattan / highball

Try a small serve with vermouth or soda, adjusting sweetness and dilution to the documented style.

Serving suggestions are editorial starting points, grounded in documented strength and style; adjust to your taste.
